_README: CR-016 UI-conformance register — the EXACT counts CR-016 says were never taken.
Read by e2e/CR-016-ui-conformance.spec.ts, which measures COMPUTED STYLE in a real
browser across every sidebar destination plus two settings sub-tabs.
THE COUNTS ARE EXACT, NOT CEILINGS — the same discipline as
10-scripts/gates/surface_debt.txt. A count going UP means a new violation shipped.
A count going DOWN means someone FIXED something and did not lower the register,
and that is red too: 'a register that keeps claiming debt it has paid off is how a
gate stops being a gate' (DEF-077). Either way the edit is a reviewable diff.
⚠ EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS NOW AT ITS CONFORMING VALUE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF A
RATCHET: the register no longer records debt, it records the shape of the design
system, so the FIRST screen that breaks any of it turns this file red. Lowered
here in the same commit as the fixes, which is what the discipline requires.
WHAT EACH NUMBER MEANS, and which authority it answers to:
nativeSelects        — <select> whose computed `appearance` is not `none`, i.e.
the browser painting its own control over ours.
B14 rule 8 (dropdowns share ONE chevron style).
26 → 0: DEF-302's fix reached `.input` selects only;
cf0423f widened it to `.view`, and the two shared
components that fought it (`.filter-select select` and
`.table-pager-size select` each set a `background`
SHORTHAND, which resets `background-image` and erased
the chevron) now carry the field kit themselves. DEF-309.
foreignControls      — a control whose computed border or background differs from
an actual `.input` injected into the same page. Compared
against the LIVE design system, never a hard-coded hex, so
retuning a token moves both sides together. 3 → 0. DEF-313.
inlineWrappingLabels — a <label> with computed display:inline that WRAPS its
control, so its text sits on the control's last baseline.
Zero here does NOT mean zero in the product: this walk
reaches list screens and settings tabs, not every panel a
click opens. It is a floor, and it is honest about that.
nonConformingKickers — .kicker elements not rendering r10's 11px/uppercase/800.
10 → 0. 26 files ask for this class, the shared PageHeader
among them, and NO app stylesheet declared it; it is now
declared once, in src/styles/global.css. DEF-308.
distinctTableBodyFontSizes / distinctTableHeaderFontSizes
— B14 rule 20: 'Table type is ONE size (13.5px) everywhere;
no inline overrides.' SIX sizes rendered (10/11/12/13/
13.5/14px); the body is now the one ratified size and the
header tier is one size too. DEF-310.
⚠ MEASURED PER ROLE SINCE 2026-08-19, and the split is a
CORRECTION, not a relaxation. Pooled into one set, the
target of 1 is unreachable by r10 ITSELF — `.table` is
13.5px and `.table th` is 11px in the same block — and
`screensWithMoreThanOneTableSize` counted a screen as
broken merely for HAVING a header, so it would have gone
UP as the product was fixed. The boundary is `thead`: a
<th> in a body row or a <tfoot> is a cell on its own line
and belongs to the body tier.
⚠ THE HEADER TIER IS 12px, NOT r10's 11px. r10 makes the
whole <th> the sort target and contains no button; our
DataTable puts a real <button class='table-sort'> inside
every sortable header, and it inherits the header size. At
11px that button is a THIRD button size on every list
screen, which B14 rule 5 forbids. Worked figure: 11px
header ⇒ 3 button sizes; 12px header ⇒ 2. Decision log
2026-08-19; raised to the PO as OQ-267.
distinctButtonFontSizes — B14 rule 5: 'Two button sizes only — default and small
(12px). No inline font sizes.' FIVE rendered; 13.3333px
was the browser's own default on `.table-columns-up`,
which no rule reached, and 15px was `.page-header-tabs
button` inheriting body copy. 5 → 2. DEF-311.
distinctControlHeights  — r10 gives `.input` ONE height (min-height 36px). FOUR
rendered; 27/33 were the shared components' near-copies of
the field kit and 38 was `input[type=date]`, whose content
box beats a min-height. 4 → 1. DEF-313.
screensWithMoreThanOneTableSize — rule 20 broken WITHIN a single page, per role.
perScreen lists only screens with a non-zero finding, and it is now EMPTY. A screen
appearing here again is a regression on the commit that adds it.
MEASURED 2026-08-19 against 08-qa/01-e2e/stack/boot_stack.sh at frontend v2.25.1,
with `npm run build` run FIRST — boot_stack serves dist/, so a stale bundle
measures yesterday's CSS.
